speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me exactly how your right groin pain started and what specific movements make it worse, and can you describe your leg's current position?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hip Fracture (likely femoral neck or intertrochanteric) secondary to a rear-end collision. The mechanism of injury, immediate onset of severe groin pain, and the need to evaluate for abnormal leg positioning are classic indicators of a femoral shaft or hip fracture rather than a soft tissue injury. Please confirm if you can bear any weight on the right leg and describe the current angle of your right leg compared to the left.
